3.

sentences.text: Only ground on which enhancement is sought for regarding monthly income of deceased being contrary to Section 4(1B) of Employee's Compensation Act (hereinafter referred to as 'E.C. Act' for short).

It was submitted that failure of award compensation towards funeral expenses was contrary to Section 4(4) of E.C.Act.
4.

It was submitted that as on date of accident i.e., 15.04.2010, deceased Tulasiram Shyamarao Satpute was 28 years of age working as coolie and earning more than `3,000/- per month with daily bhata of `50/- per day.
Therefore, Commissioner was not justified but considering it at `3,500/-.

It was further submitted that contrary to provision of Section 4(4) of E.C.Act, Commissioner NC:
2023:KHC-K:7418 erred in not awarding compensation towards funeral expenses.
5. There is no appearance on behalf of insurer.
6. Heard learned counsel for parties.
Perused impugned award.

7. From above submission, following substantial questions of law are taken-up for examination:
"(i) Whether assessment of monthly income by Commissioner is contrary to Section 4(1B) of E.C.Act ?
(ii) Whether Commissioner erred in not awarding compensation towards funeral expenses ?"
8.

Admittedly, incident has occurred on 15.04.2010 i.e., after enactment of Amending Act no.45 of 2009, inserting Section 4(1B) in of E.C.Act, whereunder, Central Government was authorized to notify income for purposes of Section 4(1).

And thereafter, Central Government issued notification no.S.O.1258(E) notifying NC: 2023:KHC-K:7418 `8,000/- as income for purposes of Sub-Section (1)
of E.C.Act, with effect from 31.05.2010.
9. Ignoring same, while passing impugned order, Commissioner determined monthly income of deceased at `6,000/-.
Same would be contrary to law.
Hence, substantial question of law no.(i) is answered in affirmative by holding that `8,000/- has to be taken as monthly income of deceased.
10. Likewise, in view of amendment to Section 4(4) of E.C.Act, in case of death, funeral expenses at not less than Rs.5,000/- has to be awarded.

Normally, in case of death under Motor Vehicles Act,
sum of `15,000/- is awarded towards funeral expenses.
Hence, same has to be awarded.

Thus,
failure to award funeral expenses would be contrary to Section 4(4) of E.C.Act.

Therefore,
substantial question of law no.(ii) has to be answered in affirmative.

11. In view of above findings, compensation awardable would be `8,47,160/- (`8,000 X 50% X NC:
2023:KHC-K:7418 211.79).
To said amount, claimants would also be entitled for `15,000/- towards funeral expenses.
